recognitionRules: Use a strong month heading and a rounded display invitation.
Keep each day’s prompt brief enough to leave writing space.
Separate planned practice from completed practice through labels, not celebratory scores.
Use repeating peach, mint and lavender weekday header cells over a fine gray seven-column calendar; retain the circle, wedge, square and zigzag source motif as a small companion.

writingLinks.name: Conversational micro-essay
writingLinks.reason: Light prompts and open space for a brief reflective habit.

quote: A little time. One small experiment. Something worth noticing.
rightsSummary: Original fictional identity and vector logos; portable font binaries retain their licenses. Source family dependencies and substitutions are documented.
logoDirection: Use MAKE ROOM TO TRY as a rounded typographic stack with one deliberately open square beneath it. The square is writing space, not a checkbox.
invariants: Use a strong month heading and a rounded display invitation.
Keep each day’s prompt brief enough to leave writing space.
Separate planned practice from completed practice through labels, not celebratory scores.
adaptations: Weekly editions can enlarge seven prompts without changing their tone.
Leave blank days available for the user’s own practice.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
